handbookNote: Wisconsin Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Wisconsin previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only wi_re_salesperson. Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services (DSPS) Real Estate Examining Board (REEB). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading and reading Pearson VUE's own official Wisconsin Real Estate Broker Candidate Handbook and Content Outlines (fetched from pearsonvue.com/content/dam/VUE/vue/en/documents/publications/095000.pdf and 095006.pdf). UNIQUE SCOPE NOTE, consistent with this site's pre-existing wi_re_salesperson track's own established, disclosed convention: unlike every other state in this campaign, this track models ONLY Wisconsin's State-specific exam portion (100 items for Broker) -- it deliberately excludes the separate National/General portion Pearson VUE also administers alongside it, matching the scope wi_re_salesperson already uses. Exam mechanics, PRIMARY-CONFIRMED from the handbook: 100 items, 3 hours 15 minutes (11,700 seconds), passing is a scaled score of 75. Consistent with this site's own pre-existing wi_re_salesperson track_registry convention (140 items, pass_percent=75, min_correct=105 -- an exact 75%-of-item-count simplification of the real scaled score), this track's DB row models pass_percent=75, min_correct=75 (100 x 0.75 = 75 exactly) as a disclosed simplification of the real scaled-score system, not a literal item-for-item passing count. CONTENT OUTLINE, quoted from Pearson VUE's own Content Outline (Broker column, 100 items across 6 sections): I. Real Estate Practice, 19 items (Licenses; Trust accounts; Duties of licensees; Confirmation/disclosure of relationships; Firms serving multiple clients; Common-law duty changes; Disclosures/investigations/inspections; Sex offender registry disclosure; Condominium disclosure; Firm/licensee responsibilities; Name/address/trade-name changes). II. Trust Accounts, 12 items (REEB 18, 18 lettered subsections A-Q covering account structure, recordkeeping, disbursement, and the $300 personal-funds cushion). III. Conduct and Ethical Practices for Real Estate Licensees, 22 items (REEB 24). IV. Approved Forms and Legal Advice, 6 items (REEB 16, the 12 named Wisconsin WB-series approved forms and the unauthorized-practice-of-law boundary). V. Drafting and Supervision Knowledge, 37 items -- the LARGEST section by a wide margin (the 12 named WB forms' individual clauses/contingencies, Wis. Stat. ch. 709 real estate condition/vacant-land/new-construction disclosure reports including the 2023-reorganized sections 709.001/.01-.08/.033/.035, and firm recordkeeping obligations). VI. Miscellaneous, 4 items (Wisconsin and federal Fair Housing Law -- Wis. Stat. Sec. 106.50 -- and the federal pre-1978 lead-based-paint disclosure rule, 42 U.S.C. Sec. 4852d). This bank's bucket sizing is directly proportional to these real, Pearson-VUE-published item weights, not an even split. Real Wisconsin statute/administrative-code facts independently verified this session via docs.legis.wisconsin.gov (Wisconsin's official Revisor of Statutes / Administrative Code site, current through 2025 Wis. Act 247) -- Wis. Stat. ch. 452 (Real Estate Practice -- Secs. 452.12, 452.132, 452.133, 452.134, 452.135, 452.139, 452.23), Wis. Admin. Code REEB 15/16/17/18/24, Wis. Stat. ch. 709 (Condition Reports), and Wis. Stat. Sec. 106.50 (Wisconsin's Open Housing/Fair Housing Law, notably broader than federal law in protected classes including sexual orientation) plus 42 U.S.C. Sec. 4852d (federal lead-based-paint disclosure). Standard national real-estate practice content not tied to a Wisconsin-specific statute is out of scope for this state-only track by design. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate. This bank was initially drafted across 6 parallel single-topic passes (one per Pearson VUE content-outline section) using this campaign's corrected no-target/no-ceiling drafting policy from the start. The initial draft (201 questions) came in well below the standing 4:1 new-track floor (100-item exam), triggering an immediate 6-agent backfill round: Real Estate Practice 50->102 (then -4 after cross-bucket dedup, see below), Trust Accounts 47->59, Conduct and Ethical Practices 41->71, Approved Forms and Legal Advice 20->33, Drafting and Supervision Knowledge 37->58 (this pass's own report flagged that it stopped short of full exhaustion due to a WebSearch budget limit, not a genuine content ceiling -- a disclosed, known gap, not silently presented as complete), Miscellaneous 6->29 (this pass explicitly reported hitting a genuine content ceiling on its narrow authorities -- Sec. 106.50 and the federal lead-paint rule -- fully exhausted). A cross-bucket source_note-citation dedup check across all 6 post-backfill files found 4 genuine near-duplicates between Real Estate Practice and Trust Accounts (all four testing the same REEB 18.032/18.05/18.10(2)/18.11 trust-account mechanics with near-identical framing) -- all four were removed from Real Estate Practice and kept in Trust Accounts, the more natural topical home, bringing Real Estate Practice from 102 to 98. FINAL TOTAL: 348 questions against a 100-item exam -- a 3.48:1 pool ratio, BELOW the standing 4:1 new-track floor. ROUND 2 BACKFILL (2026-09-02): user initially accepted the 3.48:1 shortfall as an exception, then asked to run the three most promising buckets again once specific leads were named. All 6 files were de-rotated back to the choice_a-correct convention (scripts/tracks/derotate_wi_re_broker_answers.js) and relaunched with no ceiling: Drafting and Supervision Knowledge 58->75 (closed most of its disclosed WebSearch-budget gap -- covered 15 previously-untested named WB forms plus the final two untested Wis. Stat. ch. 709 sections -- but explicitly could NOT verify WB-11's own internal contingency-clause text, since that content lives behind the Wisconsin REALTORS Association's members-only login wall with no public mirror; this one piece remains a genuinely unreachable gap, not a refused one), Trust Accounts 58->65 (live-verified every remaining REEB 18 subsection word-for-word and found only 6 genuinely untested facts left -- a real, fully-exhausted ceiling, not under-effort), Approved Forms and Legal Advice 33->40 (live-verified all of REEB 16 and Wis. Stat. Sec. 452.40 -- also a real, fully-exhausted ceiling). A fresh cross-bucket dedup check across all 6 post-round-2 files found ZERO new near-duplicates. FINAL TOTAL: 378 questions against a 100-item exam -- a 3.78:1 pool ratio, still below the 4:1 floor but backed by concrete, independently-verified evidence from all three targeted buckets that the shortfall is a genuine content ceiling (Wisconsin's state-only REEB rule set and named-form structure is simply a smaller universe than most other states' broker content outlines), not an effort gap -- accepted as the track's practical ceiling for now. Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_wi_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 6 bucket files combined, in file order), producing a final near-even 25.1/25.1/24.9/24.9% A/B/C/D distribution.
